title: Attention Sees, MLP Refuses: Tracing the Attention-to-MLP Safety Pathway in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.13078v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreaks and can over-refuse benign requests. Understanding these failures requires distinguishing harmfulness recognition from the computation that writes refusal. We reframe this as a pathway question and make it measurable on residual-stream updates in decoder-only Transformers, separating the harmfulness information a module update exposes from the change it produces in readable refusal evidence. Across 18 Base-Instruct pairs spanning Qwen, Llama, and Gemma, harmfulness is decoded more readily from attention updates, particularly in early layers, whereas MLP updates contribute more strongly to harm-selective refusal writing in aligned models. Post-training strengthens MLP refusal writing in all 18 pairs without systematically improving harmfulness decodability, while positive MLP writing becomes more concentrated in deeper layers after post-training. translated_title: 注意力负责识别，MLP负责拒绝：追踪大语言模型中从注意力到MLP的安全路径
translated_abstract: 安全对齐的大语言模型（LLM）仍然容易受到越狱攻击，并且可能过度拒绝良性请求。理解这些失败需要将有害性识别与生成拒绝的计算区分开来。我们将这一问题重新构建为一个路径问题，并使其在仅解码器Transformer的残差流更新上可测量，从而将模块更新所暴露的有害性信息与其在可读拒绝证据上产生的变化分离开来。在涵盖Qwen、Llama和Gemma的18个Base-Instruct模型对中，有害性更容易从注意力更新中被解码出来，尤其是在早期层，而MLP更新在对齐模型中对伤害选择性拒绝写入的贡献更大。后训练在所有18个模型对中增强了MLP的拒绝写入能力，但并未系统性提升有害性的可解码性，同时正向MLP写入在后训练后变得更集中于更深的层。
tldr: 该研究揭示了LLM安全机制中的分工路径：注意力模块（尤其早期层）主要负责“看见”有害信息，MLP模块主要负责“写出”拒绝输出，且后训练会增强MLP的拒绝写入能力但不会提升有害性识别能力。
en_tdlr: This study traces the safety pathway in LLMs, showing that attention modules (especially in early layers) "see" harmfulness while MLP modules "write" refusal, and post-training strengthens MLP refusal writing without improving harmfulness decodability.
